chapter_intro: The Lovers Yearn for Each Other Again.

passages.title: The Lovers Yearn for Each Other Again.
passages.text: The dream of 3:1–6:3 is over. The man and woman now offer words of praise to each other.

notes.text: This description of the woman’s beauty echoes that of 4:1–7 (see her description of the man in 5:10–16). They take romantic delight in each other’s physical appearance.
As in 4:4, the woman’s neck is likened to a tower made of precious ivory. The dignity and beauty of her neck inspires the comparison.
In ancient literature, a person of elegance was often compared to a palm tree.
The context indicates that desire here refers to sexual desire. The thought of the man desiring her gives the shepherdess pleasure.
It is possible that mandrakes (which sounds like my beloved in Hebrew) were seen as an aphrodisiac (see Gen. 30:14–16). Here, they appear to be seductive as they give forth fragrance.
